reviews.title: This is a scam
reviews.text: Here’s how it works: you sign up for an auto renew subscription. They lure you in with “discounts” for the first month and then it’s $40 a month after that. They promise to work on your cases, and they do… but it takes weeks or months to get paid from them. All the while you’re paying $40/month. If and when you ever get a settlement you’re just breaking even. Stay away from this place.

reviews.title: Scam- DO NOT SIGN UP
reviews.text: This app was advertised on social media, they have very convincing ads, they give you a survey that makes it look incredibly easy to sign up for class action suits you qualify for then they take you to a paywall- once you create a login it requires you to download the app and then you’re required to have a “passkey” to login- nothing was sent to my email and my email/password did not work when I created my account. Now I have $70 charged to my Apple ID- no clue where this charge came from, I did NOT agree to paying this much for anything on this site- for an app that I have no way of signing into, even on browser, it says email not found and then it’s as if I never made an account. I have no way of logging in and being able to cancel anything. I hope someone sees this review before they sign up and avoids the crazy $70 charge to their account for receiving absolutely nothing. Absolutely wild scam!

reviews.title: Filed claims Nothing Yet.
reviews.text: I thought signing up for this service would make filing claims faster. I am still waiting for any payout I used to just search up line for class actions, sign up and sometime in the future I would get a check. It didn’t cost me anything. Now I pay a 1/4ly fee still enter the information am still waiting for any payout.  The only good thing about Money Pilot so far is finding the claims is easier than a google search. I’m going to stick with it a little longer to see if i ever receive a payout. If I do and Money Pilot lives up its promise I’ll edit this review. So far  not worth the money.

reviews.title: Finally, an Opportunity I Qualify For: Paying MoneyPilot
reviews.text:
MoneyPilot is less of a financial app and more of an elaborate practical joke with a subscription attached.

The formula is brilliant:

Step 1: Show you a buffet of interesting financial opportunities.

Step 2: Get you to sign up.

Step 3: Reveal that you’re apparently eligible for absolutely nothing.

Step 4: Quietly keep the subscription alive until you forget this app ever existed.

Step 5: SURPRISE! Attempt to renew it.

The irony of an app called “MoneyPilot” using this business model is almost too perfect. I suppose technically they are helping manage your money—by attempting to move some of it from your account to theirs.

The opportunities are the bait. The subscription appears to be the product.

If there were an opportunity inside MoneyPilot called “Pay MoneyPilot for Access to Things You Can’t Use,” I’d finally qualify for something.

One star for successfully teaching me an important lesson about personal finance: check your subscriptions.

reviews.title: Thieves
reviews.text: I signed up for this app and asked almost immediately for a refund, because I never heard back about the lawsuits I signed up for and in fact they disappeared any record of me signing up for it. Numerous bait and switches were used and despite me asking for my money back they doubled down and charged me for a full year. I am still fighting. My can refunded me but they convinced PayPal that they are in the right. I will send PayPal the screenshots of our emails and keep fighting but it’s costing me time and money. These people are wicked and slimy. BEWARE

reviews.title: I cannot get into the app and I already paid
reviews.text: I have been trying to log into the app for over two weeks now. I have already paid for my subscription and I don’t understand why I cannot get into the app. It allows me to put my email in and after I put it in it pops up as if I still don’t have a subscription. I don’t understand what is going on right now. But I am pretty upset because it took my money with no problem and then now I just can’t login.

reviews.title: TOTAL SCAM - DO NOT PURCHASE
reviews.text: This is a basic bait and switch.  They’ll present you all the money you’re entitled to, and even have you sign the claim forms, but you have to join in order for them to process it.  This originally seemed legit and they were offering a service.  Then all your claims disappear and you can neither recover them nor see the same claims still available to file for again.   Total scam….don’t waste your time nor your money!  I had to call Apple directly to get a refund.

reviews.title: Social Media Ad Cash Grab
reviews.text:
Very convincing advertisements going around for this via social media. Random hidden additional fees when signing up. Misleading information regarding lame and pay outs. The app is very oversold as useful when in fact it barely functions and offers little to no customer support. 

Definitely built to capitalize on taking as much money as possible from users up front while providing next to zero real use or purpose.

reviews.title: I wish I read the reviews before
reviews.text: Exactly as my title says. I wish I read the reviews before. This app can find an active class action suit but in order to claim any funds even if it doesn’t require proof you need a claim number. This is an absolute scam, and they love playing the “We’ll upgrade you and give you more money for a small fee” game. Don’t fall for this go in your emails and check if there are any claim you have by searching.

reviews.title: Completely worthless
reviews.text: If you feel the inclination to spend 1999 to see if you can make $1000 don’t waste your time this app is completely worthless. Anything that I thought or their adds delusionally put in my mind that I could claim on, is not even available and you need to have so much documentation you would never get to the end of the form before giving up don’t waste your time.
